title: Elevated work platform pre-use checks
audience: Operators, spotters and supervisors on any job where an elevated work platform is planned, including exterior and window or pressure work.
learningOutcomes: Carry out a pre-use walk-round of an elevated work platform covering the machine, the basket, the controls, the ground and the overhead hazards.
Name the operator's three main duties before a platform is used.
Identify the conditions that stop a platform from being used.
Explain the fall-protection rule for a platform occupant and why the lanyard is attached to the basket.

instruction.heading: What a MEWP is
instruction.body: A MEWP, also called an elevated work platform, is a machine that lifts people and their tools. Common types include scissor lifts and boom-type platforms, which can be self-propelled, truck-mounted, tow-behind, push-around, or static booms. The sources list the hazards as falls from the basket, falling objects or people, crush injuries, electrocution, tipping, ground collapse, wind, collisions, equipment failure, and suspension trauma after a fall. Each one has a control in the pre-use check.

instruction.heading: The operator's three duties
instruction.body: One source describes three jobs for the operator. The first is to make sure the machine can be used safely. The second is to check overhead, ground and surrounding hazards. The third is to operate the machine safely. The jobs run in that order, and the operation stage does not start until the first two are complete.

instruction.heading: The machine walk-round
instruction.body: Before the first use each day, walk round the machine. Look at the wheels and tyres, the toe boards plus the guardrails, any hydraulic leak, the structure, the hoses and the wiring. Check that the controls work from the base and from the basket, as the maker's instructions describe, and that the emergency controls at the base work. Check the safe working load and the number of occupants the platform allows, and check that the labels and decals are present and readable. A machine with a defect that affects safety is tagged and kept from use. Use the maker's schedule and the business's records.

instruction.heading: Overhead and ground hazards
instruction.body: Look up before a boom is unfolded. Overhead lines, other equipment, branches and structures can contact the platform. Treat every overhead line as live until its owner or the network confirms otherwise. Check the ground: the machine must stand on a firm and flat base, and the worker should look for buried services, soft or loose ground and holes. Walk the route before driving, and watch where the machine is heading. Wind is a hazard that can tip a platform, and the wind limit is set by the maker.

instruction.heading: Inside the basket
instruction.body: Remain inside the basket. Do not climb on guardrails, and do not stand on the rails or mid-rail. A worker in the basket wears a harness connected to the basket anchorage by a restraint lanyard, as one source requires, and the maker's guidance sets the lanyard style. Keep the work within the basket's reach limits. Set up barriers, a spotter and an exclusion zone for people below. Discuss the rescue plan before the platform is raised, and read the operator's manual for each model before first use.

instruction.heading: Driving and operating
instruction.body: Drive a self-propelled platform in the lowered position where the maker allows, because that is the safest position for travel. Only a trained and competent operator may operate the machine. Keep watching where the machine is heading. Keep to the maker's load and slope limits. Tipping is the risk that the limits exist to prevent.

instruction.heading: When the platform stops being safe
instruction.body: Stop, and lower the platform, if a control becomes unreliable, a warning light or alarm activates, the ground moves, the wind rises, a person is hurt, or a line is contacted. If the platform contacts a power line, the business's emergency procedure applies. The power must be isolated before anyone moves or touches the machine.

procedure: Confirm the operator is trained and authorised for this machine type and size.
Complete the walk-round and record any defect.
Check the controls from the base and from the basket.
Look up and check overhead hazards, and keep the clearance the business plan requires.
Check the ground, choose the spot, and set outriggers or stabilisers as the maker requires.
Set an exclusion zone and a spotter where people could be below.
Attach the harness and restraint lanyard to the basket anchorage before the basket rises.
Operate within the limits, and stop when conditions change.
Lower and secure the platform at the end of the job, and record any defect found.

workedExamples.situation: A worker plans to use a self-propelled boom platform on a footpath beside a house, with an overhead power line about four metres above the boom.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Can the job go ahead on this basis?
workedExamples.reasoning: Not on this basis. The overhead line must be assessed against the business plan and the network rules, and the footpath may need an exclusion zone and a spotter. The job does not start until the line question is answered, and until the operator and the machine are confirmed against the licence position in this lesson.

workedExamples.situation: A scissor lift has a slightly low tyre, and a warning light comes on during the walk-round.
workedExamples.reasoning: The machine is tagged and kept out of use, and the defect is reported. A warning light is a stop condition until the cause has been identified and the maker's repair has been completed and checked. The machine is not used on another job until the fault is cleared.

equipmentAndPpe: Harness with a restraint lanyard for the basket
Operator's manual and load chart for the model

commonErrors.error: Skipping the walk-round because the machine was used the day before.
commonErrors.prevention: Walk the machine round before each day's first use. The check is per day, not per job.

commonErrors.error: Standing on the guardrail to reach further.
commonErrors.prevention: Reposition the platform. Remain inside the basket.
Lower the platform for travel where the maker allows, and watch where the machine is heading.

commonErrors.error: Assuming a line is dead because it appears de-energised.
commonErrors.prevention: Treat every overhead line as live until confirmed by its owner or the network.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Warning: a platform with a defect that affects safety must be tagged out of use until it has been repaired and checked.
Warning: keep clear of overhead lines, and treat each one as live until its owner or the network confirms otherwise.

Licence notice: a high risk work licence is required to operate boom-type platforms in Victoria, where the WP class has no boom-length threshold; in New South Wales where the boom is 11 metres or more; in Queensland, where platforms under 11 metres are excluded, so a shorter boom may not need it; in Tasmania where the boom is 11 metres or more (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023); and in Western Australia and the Northern Territory where the boom is 11 metres or more. A scissor lift does not need a high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start.
This lesson does not grant a licence, operator competence or any authority to operate a platform. Completing it does not qualify any worker to operate a platform.
The business plan and the maker's documents govern until they are checked.

qualityStandard: A walk-round is recorded for each day, with any defect found.
Overhead and ground checks are recorded before the platform rises.
The harness and restraint lanyard are connected before the basket is raised.
Operator authority is checked against the business register.
summary: Check the machine, the overhead lines and the ground before the platform rises.
Remain inside the basket, with the harness connected before the basket goes up.
Stop and lower the platform when a control, a line, the ground or the wind is wrong.
The licence position depends on the state and the boom length, and must be checked first.

knowledgeChecks.question: Before first use on a day, which check is required for a platform?
options: None; the platform is checked once a year only and the operator checks the paint
A walk-round covering the machine, guardrails, controls, ground and overhead hazards.
Only a check that the engine starts and the battery is charged and the tyres are full
Only a check of the lowering controls and the tyres and the paint are checked

knowledgeChecks.question: A line that appears to be switched off is overhead. What should the operator assume?
options: That it is dead because the power is off in the building
That it is live until the owner or the network confirms otherwise.
That it is insulated and safe to touch and the cover is on it
That the wind will carry it away and it will fall away from the van

knowledgeChecks.question: Under the sources, which of these is a condition that stops use of a platform?
options: A defect that affects safety, such as a warning alarm or a damaged control.
The operator wearing gloves and a hat and boots on the day in the sun
The machine being clean and the paint being bright and shiny for the day
Working during daylight, when visibility is at its best on a clear day.
